title: America's Godly Heritage Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of America's founding and the role of faith in our nation's history!

questions.question: What did Christopher Columbus name his first landing place, and what does it mean?
questions.explanation: Columbus named his first landing place 'San Salvador,' meaning 'Holy Savior,' to thank God for guiding him safely across the ocean.

questions.question: Why did the Pilgrims leave England and sail to America?
options: To explore new lands for the king
To worship God freely according to the Bible
questions.explanation: The Pilgrims left England because they were not allowed to worship God the way they believed the Bible taught. They came to America seeking religious freedom.

questions.question: What was the Mayflower Compact?
options: A map of the New World
An agreement to govern themselves under God's laws
A letter to the King of England
questions.explanation: The Mayflower Compact was an agreement the Pilgrims wrote to govern themselves based on Biblical principles of covenant and community. It was one of the first examples of self-government in America.

questions.question: According to the Declaration of Independence, where do our rights come from?
questions.explanation: The Declaration of Independence states that all people 'are endowed by their Creator with certain unalienable Rights.' This means our rights come from God, not from any government.

questions.question: Which Bible verse inspired the Founders to create three branches of government?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 33:22 describes God as judge, lawgiver, and king — three roles that inspired the three branches of government: Judicial, Legislative, and Executive.

questions.question: Why did the Founders divide the government into three branches?
options: Because three is a lucky number
Because the Bible teaches that people are sinners and no one should have too much power
Because there were three original colonies
questions.explanation: The Founders knew from the Bible that all people are sinners (Romans 3:23), so they divided the government into three branches to prevent any one person or group from gaining too much power.

questions.question: What is the official motto of the United States?
questions.explanation: 'In God We Trust' is the official national motto of the United States, reflecting America's heritage of faith in God.

questions.question: Which Founding Father called the delegates at the Constitutional Convention to prayer?
questions.explanation: Benjamin Franklin called the delegates to prayer, saying, 'I have lived, sir, a long time, and the longer I live the more convincing proofs I see of this truth — that God governs in the affairs of men.'
